glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: test | Severity: medium
  File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/tests/unit/real-variant.spec.ts:106 (titles map)
  Finding: `titles: { 1: ..., 2: ..., 3: ... }` maps the fresh id (1) and the drafted id (2) to the *same* pricing title. The test can no longer detect if the wrong thread is opened for a given status — clicking the "new" row (onboarding title) would still pass, because the fresh id is mapped to the drafted thread's title. The old test mapped distinct titles per status and thus actually discriminated. The inline comment acknowledges this ("id 3 is never opened") but doesn't justify collapsing fresh and drafted.
  Suggestion: If the static mockup only ever renders one detail thread, restrict the state to what the page can actually show (e.g. only assert the drafted thread) rather than mapping two different status ids to one title, so a regression that opens the wrong row fails loudly.

- Category: spec | Severity: low
  File: integration-tests/fixtures/social-engagement-real/mockups/02-thread.html (third comment)
  Finding: The spec says "Layout, CSS and structure are unchanged", but the comment nesting changed: the old markup was `comment → comment d1 → comment d2` (a nested reply chain); the new markup is `comment → comment d1 → comment` (flat with one indented reply). If the "comments joined" rule is genuinely a flat join, this is correct data-driven behavior, but it contradicts the "structure unchanged" claim and slightly changes rendered indentation/occupancy.
  Suggestion: Either confirm the recorded data has no nested replies (and note the structure change in the run doc), or keep the nesting classes consistent with what the real backend renders for reply threads.

- Category: test | Severity: low
  File: integration-tests/e2e-webui/tests/unit/real-variant.spec.ts:136
  Finding: The S02 state still declares `posted: 1, drafted: 1, fresh: 1` but supplies a title only for id 1. If the harness resolves titles for the other ids when verifying status labels, the missing entries will be `undefined`; if it doesn't, the posted/drafted counts are unverified. Either way the assertion strength is unclear.
  Suggestion: Supply titles for every id the harness will read, or trim the state to the ids actually exercised.

## Checks that passed

- The `package_sha256` pin was updated together with the changed mockups (AC2 mechanism present; actual hash correctness can only be verified by `test_e2e_real_fixture.py`, which the spec says covers it).
- Switcher counts 4/4/4, list rows, status labels, and the "12 new hits added" note are consistent across all five mockups and match the spec table.
- Summary derivation (first sentence as question, joined comments, fixed angle line) is consistently applied on 02/03/04.
- 01-board and 05-sources correctly show no per-thread detail and keep the expired row in the list.
- No security concerns — static HTML fixture with fixed strings.

Overall: the fixture work matches the spec; the only substantive concern is that the unit test's title mapping was weakened so it can no longer distinguish which thread a click reveals. Ship-with-fixes (the test-mapping fix is small; the rest is acceptable).

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
